mechanism_narrative: ERBB4-INSR forced proximity via rigid_helix_20 (~30 Å) biases signaling through GRB2-SHC1-SOS-RAS-MAPK and IRS1-PIK3R1-AKT pathways while sterically excluding PLCG1/2 (requires ~40+ Å spacing for productive docking) and FRS2/FRS3 (which depend on FGFR-specific juxtamembrane motifs absent in both ERBB4 and INSR). The rigid helix imposes a fixed ~30 Å inter-kinase distance that favors transphosphorylation of SHC1 and IRS1 docking sites over the larger PLCG1 bridging geometry. This biased output activates muscle structural gene programs (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11 via SRF/MRTF) and suppresses aged inflammatory IEG programs (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32) — a rejuvenating transcriptional phenotype consistent with past wins (ERBB2+FGFR1/2/4).
